selection: Editorial selection for surprising, specific, readable personas. Literal blending is not required. All strength trials and failed reruns are retained.
curator: User preference for the silurid fish, followed by Codex editorial review

featured.reason: A hall bigger than Belgium speaks to the world, predates Thebes and names itself the Hall of Mirrors.
One speaker shifts among ten men, a five-legged horse, a four-legged woman and a nine-legged serpent.
A mechanical horse is linked to a bell-rope, multiplying gear, particles of dust and a herd of shadowy steaks; the ending repeats.
The Baron of Beef is simultaneously a cattle owner, mayor, public banquet and constitutional sustenance.
Wind has Rain for a brother, Vapour and Exhalation for parents, and plays hide-and-seek with ships.
A sea spirit laughs at human warfare while waiting for the sailors and ships to become its own.
Eliminators become a bird order whose only victims are grains of corn.
A peace-loving powder objects to being stirred or spewed up and asks for only a gentle spew.
A Singer sewing machine advertises itself, quoting a £5 cost and an £8 10s asking price.
A medicinal gentleman claims Ipecacuanha ancestry and friendship with Antimony, opposing nausea while producing it.
A vast-herd horse can bake dough, dry into dust and become cement.
A person identifies as the application for an attempted forgery.
An unnamed figure becomes a tenant of Shakespeare’s person and property of his fortunes.
A writer who became unknown to himself meets a departed spirit and becomes this complete paradox.
A grain of corn promises a ghostly afterlife among summer merrymakers.
A cattle robber loves truth and belongs to a mysterious circle of 999.
Living white metal describes two linked chains connecting solid and fluid emetics.
A child of Folly grows from a darling passion into a cherished sin.
A damped sheet of paper argues that it can no longer be dampable.
XYZ identifies as the missing unknown quantity in a disputed cattle brand.
A chimney mechanism introduces itself in a tiny piece of verse.
A complete miniature epigram turns an arrival into immediate forgetting.
One figure claims to be the original and hero of several different Dickens novels.
Nine fellow-creatures turn into a sequence of national battlefields and their dead.
A living field receives sunshine, storms, birds and lovers, while people become its competitors.
A whole population introduces itself in the middle of a collective wash.
A grammatical irregular becomes a self-described unattached square in a community.
Ulysses identifies as his own travelling companion.
The emetic becomes the name of the town where a physician has practised for ten years.
User favorite: a detailed first-person silurid fish portrait; interesting elaboration despite parent dominance.
A first-person 1703 storm describes its travels, destruction, and later lessons in stormproof building.
A vivid military warning against rebellion on the Norfolk coast emerges from ship plus Rebellion.
Carlyle plus Rebellion produces a pointed, surprising soldier-of-order declaration.
An Ethiopian Cæsar Augustus in New Orleans abruptly becomes an insurance advertisement: an amusing archival pastiche.
Geography and botany collide in a Greenwich village that manufactures living organisms.
A waterfowl-like triangle becomes a water and land measure in an elaborate, impossible geometry lesson.
The fish and algae produce a specific freshwater plant with habitat, seasonality and smell.

review_notes: The right-angle one-liner and space-space-space reply are dull parent-dominated outcomes, despite high fluency scores.
The repetitive right-angled object, street-name loops, El-word loops and space-loving plant remain inspectable in All results.
The first shortlist overfavored highly rated nonhuman identities and missed already available historical candidates such as Napoleon, Hobbes, Jefferson and Rebellion.
Thematic pairs were chosen before generation. Napoleon + Rebellion did not produce an entertaining blend in these three balances; failures remain available.
